title: Traits and ownership in Rust
summary: Implement a trait for a struct, then diagnose a use-after-move error.

scenario.briefing: A telemetry service summarizes different record types through one trait. Implement the trait and keep ownership clear.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.
Diagnose a realistic mistake and choose the correct repair.

hints: The method signature must match the trait.
Borrow self so the article remains owned by main.

misconceptions.description: Using a value after passing it by value.
misconceptions.diagnostic: The value is moved into consume and then reused after the move.
misconceptions.feedback: A move transfers ownership. Borrow with & or clone deliberately.

misconceptions.description: Treating an async call as already completed.
misconceptions.feedback: Calling an async function returns a future. Await it inside an async context.

misconceptions.description: Removing the later use instead of borrowing the value.
misconceptions.feedback: Deleting the print hides the ownership problem. Borrow with &name so the original stays usable.

sections.title: Rust functions and collections
sections.body: Functions declare parameter and return types: fn add(left: i32, right: i32) -> i32 { left + right }. Vec<i32> owns a growable array. Traits define shared behavior, and generic functions use trait bounds.

sections.title: Rust errors and tools
sections.body: Result<T, E> and the ? operator propagate failure. Async functions return futures that an executor drives. cargo build compiles, cargo test runs tests, cargo clippy checks lints, and cargo fmt formats source.

steps.title: Implement a summary trait
steps.prompt: Edit src/main.rs. Article implements Summary, and summarize returns the article title.

tests.description: The Summary trait remains the shared contract.
Article implements the trait without taking ownership of self.

hints: Match the trait method signature exactly.
Borrow self so the article remains owned by main.
impl Summary for Article { fn summarize(&self) -> String { format!("{}", self.title) } }

steps.title: Use after move
steps.prompt: This program passes a String to a function and then uses it again. Select the faulty instruction and the correct repair.

fixes.label: Pass &name to consume and borrow the string.
Pass name.clone() and keep the original.

steps.explanation: Passing name by value moves it. Borrowing with &name leaves the original owned by main.
hints: Passing a String by value moves ownership.
Using name after the move is rejected by the compiler.
Borrow with &name to keep ownership in main.

steps.title: Ownership and traits

statements.label: A trait defines behavior that types can implement.
Passing a String to a function moves ownership unless it is borrowed or cloned.
An async function runs immediately to completion when called.
Cargo can run tests and manage dependency versions.

steps.explanation: Traits define shared contracts, and ownership rules make moves explicit. Async functions return futures that must be driven.
hints: An async function returns a future; it does not run to completion when called.
